transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next. It's like I really can’t just sit idle. And, well, we recently got a new work setup at my job, and it's just made that a lot harder to hide.
Have you always felt this need to stay constantly active, even when you were a child, or is this something that has started more recently?

Well, looking back, it's been around long before this job change. Even when I was a kid... I remember back in grade school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. They always noted that I talked out of turn and constantly had to be reminded to just stay with my work. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing.

latest_inference.note: The patient's report of childhood symptoms (carelessness, talking out of turn, inability to stay with work) combined with persistent adult restlessness strongly points toward ADHD, making the other mood and anxiety-related candidates less likely.
